content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me enough to move.

Your ≈£1,250/mo of free cash is the headline. The exit pot needs ≈£40/mo to hit £1,000 by June 2028 — that's ≈2% of take-home, and it fits. The problem isn't the goal's size. It's that ≈£0/mo is currently going aside, and ≈£1,100/mo is drifting somewhere neither of us can name yet.

So the move is simple: start a standing transfer of ≈£150/mo on payday. Not the optimised number — the first one. The habit is what matters here. That's four times the pace the goal needs, which means security starts building from month one rather than month thirty.

You called the ≈£1,100/mo drift a leak. A real month settles whether that's one pattern or ten — and whether any of it is actually recurring spend in disguise.

Checking a real month does two things: it swaps every ≈ for an actual number, so you can see estimate versus reality side by side. And right now the habits half of your picture is completely empty — timing, patterns, what's recurring — because estimates can't see any of that. Only real transactions can.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
